module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Congruences $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod k$ for hypergeometric values ${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$

a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.

*References:*
- [A278070](https://oeis.org/A278070)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA278070


open Nat Finset

/--
a: $a(n) = \text{hypergeometric}([n, -n], [], -1)$.
This is equivalent to the combinatorial sum:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k-1}{k} k!$$
The expression uses $\mathbb{N}$ arithmetic throughout, safely handling
the subtraction via `Nat.pred`.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (n + 1)).sum fun k =>
    (n.choose k) * ((n + k).pred.choose k) * (k.factorial)


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 2 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 106 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 1457 := by rfl


/--
Conjecture: $a(n+k) \equiv a(n) \pmod{k}$ for all $n$ and $k$. - _Peter Bala_, Mar 12 2023

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/278070.wip.lean#L68"]
theorem a_modeq : ∀ (n k : ℕ), Nat.ModEq k (a (n + k)) (a n) := by
    sorry

end OeisA278070

findings.description: The module docstring title calls the values "${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$". The expression hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1) has two upper and zero lower parameters, so it is ${}_2F_0(n,-n;;-1)$. A ${}_2F_1$ needs exactly one lower parameter, and the empty slot in the title contradicts its own subscript. For example, ${}_2F_1(2,-2;1;-1) = 1+4+3 = 8 \ne 11 = a(2)$, while ${}_2F_0(2,-2;;-1) = 1+4+6 = 11$. The Lean definition `a` (the finite sum) correctly equals the ${}_2F_0$ value, and the def and theorem docstrings are correct. Only the module title is wrong, and the mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A278070 name line: "a(n) = hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1)." The Maple program is `hypergeom([n, -n], [], -1)`. This is Maple's generalized hypergeometric with an empty lower-parameter list, i.e. 2F0. Read via the Wayback capture https://web.archive.org/web/20260904142450id_/https://oeis.org/A278070.
findings.suggested_fix: In the module docstring title, replace "${}_2F_1(n, -n; ; -1)$" with "${}_2F_0(n, -n; ; -1)$".

reformulations.difference: The source defines a(n) = hypergeometric([n, -n], [], -1), a terminating 2F0 at -1. The Lean defines `a n` as the ℕ-valued finite sum Σ_{k=0}^{n} C(n,k)·C((n+k).pred, k)·k!, with `Nat.pred` standing in for n+k-1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The k-th term of 2F0(n,-n;;-1) is (n)_k (-n)_k (-1)^k / k!. For k ≤ n, (-n)_k (-1)^k = n!/(n-k)!. For k > n it is 0, so the series stops at k = n. For n ≥ 1, (n)_k = C(n+k-1,k)·k!, so the term is C(n,k)·C(n+k-1,k)·k!. For n ≥ 1 we have n+k-1 ≥ 0, so `Nat.pred` is exact. The only truncated case is n = k = 0, where both sides give 1: (0)_0 = 1 and C(0,0) = 1. The OEIS entry lists exactly this sum as a formula (Peter Luschny, May 31 2026). Gutkovskiy's formula n![x^n] e^x/(1-x)^n expands to the same sum. `#eval` in a scratch file matches all 371 terms of the OEIS b-file (n = 0..370).

review.notes:
Checks done:
(1) Definition: `a n` equals the OEIS b-file value for every n = 0..370 (`#eval`). The test lemmas `a_0`–`a_4` match the OEIS data.
(2) Statement: `a_modeq` states Bala's conjecture a(n+k) ≡ a(n) (mod k) for all n, k ≥ 0. This is the natural reading at offset 0; Adamczewski's OEIS Open paper also reads it as "all nonnegative integers n, k". The case k = 0 is trivially true, since `Nat.ModEq 0` is equality and a(n+0) = a(n). A numerical check for n, k < 80 passes. The mod-7 residues [1,2,4,1,1,4,2,...] match the OEIS example.
(3) Provability: I adapted Epoch's independent proof to the file's own `OeisA278070.a`. The only edit was disambiguating `Finset.antidiagonal` to `Finset.HasAntidiagonal.antidiagonal`. It compiles against this checkout with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], and `theorem same_type : @OeisA278070.a_modeq = file_statement_holds := rfl` typechecks. So the exact statement is proved, and `research solved` is correct. The OEIS records the first conjecture as proved by an AI agent (Ralf Stephan, May 31 2026).
(4) The AlphaProof Nexus proof linked from the OEIS has a verbatim-identical definition and statement. Its golfed proof no longer compiles on this Mathlib: the lemma `Nat.succ_mul_choose_eq` does not exist here, and the `hint` step fails. This is version drift only.
(5) I did not open the `formal_proof` URL, which points to the fork github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures. I stayed away from it to respect the prohibition on consulting the formal-conjectures repository on GitHub. So I have not checked that line 68 of that .wip.lean file is the right declaration. The claim itself (the statement is formally proved) is confirmed by (3). Linking to that fork with kind `formal_conjectures` is a widespread convention in this repository: 83 occurrences under FormalConjectures/.
(6) The same OEIS comment also poses a more general conjecture: b(n) = n![x^n] exp(x G(x)) F(x)^n satisfies b(n+k) ≡ b(n) (mod k) for integer power series F, G with F(0) = G(0) = 1. The file does not formalize it. This is an omitted variant, not a misformalization. Per the OEIS, only the first conjecture has been proved.
